title: A Combined Pore Blockage and Cake Filtration Model for Protein Fouling during Microfiltration

model_assumptions.text: Rate of pore coverage proportional to convective flow rate of protein aggregates.
model_assumptions.quote: The rate of pore coverage or blockage is assumed to be proportional to the convective flow rate of protein aggregates to the membrane surface.

model_assumptions.text: Each aggregate blocks a given membrane area.
model_assumptions.quote: Each aggregate is assumed to block a given area of membrane ( $ A_{agg} $).

model_assumptions.text: Initial deposit is partially permeable, allowing some flow through blocked pores.
model_assumptions.quote: This initial deposit is assumed to be at least partially permeable to fluid flow, i.e., there is some small finite flow through even the “blocked” pores.

model_assumptions.text: Deposit hydraulic resistance proportional to mass per unit area.
model_assumptions.quote: The hydraulic resistance of the protein deposit is assumed to be directly proportional to the mass per unit area,

model_assumptions.text: Specific protein layer resistance R' assumed constant during constant pressure filtration.
model_assumptions.quote: $ R' $ is the specific protein layer resistance, which is assumed to be constant during a constant pressure filtration.

model_assumptions.text: Deposit growth proportional to convective transport of protein through each blocked region.
model_assumptions.quote: The growth of the protein deposit over each blocked region of the membrane is assumed to be proportional to the convective transport of protein through that particular region,

model_assumptions.text: Initial deposit resistance estimated using Kozeny–Carman equation.
model_assumptions.quote: The resistance of the initial protein deposit ($R_{p0}$) can be estimated from the Kozeny–Carman equation,
